ranked.headline: Quantitative lineage and spatial structure encoded in multicellular developmental data
ranked.summary: Tracking tools and geometric models now yield parameterized, relational readouts of developmental mode from single-cell and chromatin data.

ranked.headline: Single-cell computational methods link cell states to disease and drug response
ranked.summary: Population-scale single-cell atlases and sample-level methods now attribute communication, drug response and disease trajectories to specific cell states.

ranked.headline: Structure-constrained encoders now align and integrate spatial and single-cell omics
ranked.summary: Contrastive, graph, and transport encoders are now applied to spatial and single-cell omics with explicit biological or geometric constraints.

ranked.headline: Simulations resolve residue-level recognition and conformational gating in complexes
ranked.summary: Recent MD and structure-based modeling studies pinpoint which residues and conformational states govern binding in RNA and protein complexes.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking computational tools against reference data across transcriptomic datasets
ranked.summary: Benchmarks against defined reference sets now anchor validation of tools spanning scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and long-read RNA-seq.

ranked.headline: Non-additive genetics and pathway modeling extend GWAS toward functional interpretation
ranked.summary: Recent work extends association testing to non-additive effects, co-expression, and metabolic gene mapping in large biobank cohorts.

ranked.headline: Perturbation response models are assessed by generalizability and in vivo transport
ranked.summary: Sparse and heterogeneous perturbation data now test whether in vitro and single-cell predictions hold for patients and new contexts.

ranked.headline: Deep learning and language models decode proteomic, channel, and enzyme data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply ESM-2 embeddings and deep learning to peptide spectra, proteoforms, and ion channels, alongside a review of enzyme kinetic models.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics fusion and graph embeddings predict BRAF inhibitor response in cell lines
ranked.summary: Benchmarks of single-cell foundation models and encoding choices now test whether response prediction generalizes beyond bulk cell lines.

ranked.headline: Gene-expression profiles feed ML models linking genes to cell types and patient outcomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair single-cell and bulk transcriptomes with ML to map disease phenotypes, predict responses, and resolve regulatory contacts.

ranked.headline: Embedding design criteria into generative and selection loops for molecular discovery
ranked.summary: Guidance and selection strategies are being built into molecular generative and selection loops rather than applied only after candidates are proposed.

ranked.headline: Auditing fungal and viral reference genomes to make comparative inference reliable
ranked.summary: Recent preprints curate and audit fungal and viral reference genomes, targeting assembly quality and metadata before comparative analysis.

ranked.headline: Graph and language-model representations advance drug-target interaction prediction
ranked.summary: Recent papers and preprints pair graph architectures with pretrained or learned representations to address scarce labels and practical benchmark design.

ranked.headline: Latent neural representations across spatial scales, modalities, and recording types
ranked.summary: Large-scale fMRI, iEEG, spike, LFP, and week-long clinical recordings now enable self-supervised latent models of heterogeneous neural data.

ranked.headline: Pretrained histology models are being coupled with genomic, text and spatial omics data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair large histology and spatial pretraining with genomic, text and prior-knowledge inputs across cancer tasks.

ranked.headline: Structure encodings under test for predicting protein and ligand binding affinity
ranked.summary: Benchmarks of co-folding, docking, and refolding pipelines expose where current structure predictors and encodings fail for design and affinity tasks.

ranked.headline: Learned denoising and self-supervision recover structure from noisy bioimaging data
ranked.summary: Data-driven reconstruction now recovers structure from noisy or indirect biological measurements across cryo-EM, super-resolution, MRE, and knee mechanics.

ranked.headline: Variant calling and classification choices shape mutation signatures and variant calls
ranked.summary: Consensus calling, interpretable tumour-only classifiers and guideline automation are being benchmarked for accuracy, robustness and ancestry-aware performance.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale genomes link transposon expansion and rearrangements to genome size
ranked.summary: Chromosome-level assemblies of planarians, lamprey and Physaria now resolve architecture behind genome size and vertebrate gene family evolution.

ranked.headline: Genome-wide comparisons link codon usage, gene content, and repeat evolution across taxa
ranked.summary: Large genome collections now allow selection scans and phylogenetic profiling across bacteria, gut microbiomes, and fungi at population and clade scale.

ranked.headline: Long-read and T2T profiling resolves centromere, telomere, and rDNA variation
ranked.summary: Complete and long-read genomes now resolve centromere, telomere, and rDNA variation across populations, pedigrees, and tissues.

ranked.headline: Computational methods track atom provenance and assign metabolite stereoisomer identity
ranked.summary: Structure-based tools now resolve isotopomer labelings, stereochemical identity, and biosynthetic product classes at fine resolution.

ranked.headline: Explicit E/I circuit models link network parameters to neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Explicit E/I-constrained network and imaging models now quantitatively connect circuit parameters to spectral, training, and whole-brain synchrony outcomes.

ranked.headline: Computational methods targeting disordered proteins, membrane binding, and…
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply AI design, MD, and free-energy methods to disordered, membrane, and solvent-complex systems beyond ordered folds.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale models link bacterial gene content to lineage-specific metabolic function
ranked.summary: Genome-scale models now scale to thousands of genomes and microbial consortia, moving analysis beyond single-strain reconstructions.

ranked.headline: Open tools benchmark and standardize proteomics, genomics and LC-MS data processing
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published viewer extend open-source omics tooling toward benchmarking, standardized data formats and interactive exploration.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict RNA modifications, structure, and extracellular vesicle sorting
ranked.summary: Nanopore-scale datasets and learned sequence models now resolve RNA modifications, structural states, and vesicle cargo enrichment.

ranked.headline: Correcting array and platform batch effects in methylation and genotype inference
ranked.summary: Pooled methylation and genotype inference across array and sequencing platforms now requires explicit platform-level calibration before analysis.

ranked.headline: RBP control of splicing and decay across tumor and glioma transcriptomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints tie NMD efficiency and candidate RBP regulators to tumor RNA-seq, alongside single-cell splicing atlases of glioma.

ranked.headline: Statistical estimators recover cell-state and regulatory structure from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Shallowly observed cells and million-cell datasets are pushing single-cell inference toward scalable, uncertainty-aware estimators.

ranked.headline: Coupling epidemic compartment models to behavioral, structural, and spatial feedback
ranked.summary: Recent preprints analyze how behavioral, structural, and within-host feedback enter epidemic threshold and stability results directly.

ranked.headline: Genomes resolve microbial lineage structure and trait distribution across environments
ranked.summary: Expanded isolate, metagenome-resolved, and organelle genome sampling now resolves lineage boundaries across bacteria and algae.

ranked.headline: Generative and de novo design of PROTACs, Gd-binding peptides, and protein binders
ranked.summary: Generative and de novo pipelines now address PROTAC synthesizability, Gd-binding peptides, and small-molecule-targeting protein binders.

ranked.headline: Genomic AMR prediction is confounded by sampling bias and resistance-gene call errors
ranked.summary: Long-read nanopore workflows now identify pathogens and AMR genes from blood cultures in about 4 h, raising the stakes for accurate resistance prediction.

ranked.headline: Noise constraints shape ultrasensitive gene switches and causal inference from expression
ranked.summary: Simulations and a theoretical noise-propagation relation now link fluctuation control in regulatory networks to causal gene inference.

ranked.headline: Neural parameterization of mechanistic models for reactions and cell trajectories
ranked.summary: Neural surrogates now track large reaction networks and infer ODE models from single-cell trajectories.

ranked.headline: Shared feature definitions for isoform, chromatin, and sequencing QC analysis
ranked.summary: New tools standardize analysis features for long-read, single-cell chromatin, and population sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Biophysical models link axon geometry and myelin damage to conduction and stimulation
ranked.summary: Explicit geometric and pathological detail in neuron and nerve models now predicts conduction and responses to electrical stimulation.

ranked.headline: New algorithms align sequence chains to pangenome paths and gene trees to pedigrees
ranked.summary: Recent preprints formalize alignment of sequences and trees to graph and genealogical structures, extending indexing beyond linear reference coordinates.

ranked.headline: Mass spectrometry advances deepen proteomics and resolve glycans and peptaibols
ranked.summary: Recent work extends mass spectrometry depth, identification and database-driven annotation across proteomics, glycomics and natural product analysis.
